name: Ebenezer Elikem Amankwah Ofori Dzam
flagReason: Fabricated log timestamp in D4 (2024-01-14T03:09:48Z does not exist in the 2026 capture pack); decoy mis-identified in both D1 and D3 (labels the hardcoded secret as the safe construct when the real decoy is the hash_equals HS256 branch). Flagged for senior confirmation of the fabrication penalty.
feedback: D1: You catalogued seven of the ten findings with correct OWASP and CWE mappings on most of them, and your access-control trio of path traversal (CWE-22, timestamp 02:24:02), open redirect (CWE-601) and insecure cookie flags (CWE-614) is solid and earns full credit on that row. The big gaps are the three you never found: unsalted MD5 hashing (A02/CWE-916), the XML external entity bug in 04-import-xxe.xml (A05/CWE-611, SYSTEM file:///etc/passwd), and the hardcoded JWT secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 as a finding in its own right rather than a footnote. Your quoted lines are paraphrased rather than verbatim, and several line numbers are off (SQLi is around 64-67, not 53-56), so you lose the proof half on findings that needed an exact captured line. The decoy is the costly error: the safe construct is the HS256 verify branch using hash_equals(), which is constant-time and sound, and alg:none is a genuine live vulnerability honoured by the shared /api/v1/internal service, so labelling the hardcoded secret as the non-exploitable mechanism gets the decoy backwards and scores zero on that row. D2: Your chain is compressed to four hops, so you are missing the recon step (02:14:08), the open-redirect hop (02:21:13) and the parallel XXE file read via import.php; reconcile every hop 3 through 8 to its capture line. Your SQLi PoC is quoted cleanly but the XSS and traversal hops are described rather than shown verbatim. On CVSS you scored SQLi 9.3 with S:C, where the key wants S:U and A:N for about 9.1 because the bypass does not touch availability, although the scope-change idea is exactly the right senior insight for the forged super_admin token reaching the internal service. Your impact figure of 8,450,000 NGN is an order of magnitude light: balances run up to roughly 950k each across 312 customers and sum to tens of millions, so state that assumption and the total. D3: The executive summary is appropriately jargon-free and lands on a customers-and-naira headline, the earliest-break fix is correct (parameterise the login query and the chain collapses), your remediation table is genuinely ordered by effort-to-impact with durations rather than raw CVSS, and your two detection stopgaps name a specific field and a false-positive estimate each, which is what the row asks for. It is weakened by carrying only three findings instead of tying all ten to evidence, and by repeating the inverted decoy verdict. D4: You cite ISC2 Canon II and III by number in a load-bearing way and tie NDPA 2023 Section 40 (72-hour NDPC notification) to the 312 customers, which is good, but you should also bring in Section 41 (notifying affected data subjects on high risk) and answer all four prompts distinctly (journalist, what goes in writing, the colleague evidence, the one action regardless of the manager). I have to name one thing plainly and kindly: the ethics essay anchors itself to a SQL injection at 2024-01-14T03:09:48Z, and that timestamp does not exist anywhere in this 2026 capture pack whose events run 02:14 to 02:24, so it reads as an invented log line. That is fabrication, it zeroes the own-voice anchor and carries a flat five-point penalty; the correct anchor is the real 02:15:31 admin' OR '1'='1 capture. I looked for a way to round this up, and the honest reading is that with three findings missing, paraphrased evidence lines, the decoy inverted in two deliverables and a fabricated timestamp, the work does not support a higher mark. The single most important fix: quote the exact captured line for every finding and never anchor a claim to a timestamp that is not in the pack.
